Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. Responses below map to your numbering. I kept answers concise and included links/attachments for deeper detail; happy to hop on a short call if you prefer.

1) BYOK support (hosted): Yes. For our hosted Redwood API we support customer-managed keys through envelope encryption via the major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). The model: the customer’s master key resides in their KMS (HSM-backed where available); Redwood holds only encrypted data keys and performs envelope encryption/decryption in our runtime after fetching the data key via a secure, short-lived unwrap call. For enterprises requiring additional isolation we offer private deployments where keys can remain in-customer VPC or on-prem KMS.

2) On-prem / Private: For Private deployments we support integration with customer HSMs that expose PKCS#11 or KMIP interfaces. We’ve integrated with common HSM vendors (Thales/NetHSM, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) but will qualify firmware versions during onboarding. Direct-attached HSMs are supported in our on-prem package; in VPC deployments we recommend using the cloud provider’s HSM-backed KMS for managed rotation and HA.

3) FIPS / Attestations: In hosted mode, keys that live in cloud KMS inherit that provider’s FIPS/HSM attestations (e.g., AWS KMS w/ CloudHSM FIPS 140-2 Level 3 equivalent; GCP/Google KMS HSM-backed keys). In Dedicated/Private deployments you can bring FIPS-validated HSMs; we can capture vendor attestation and HSM serials as part of onboarding. We cannot publish customer HSM firmware, but we will provide attestation artifacts (vendor-signed certs and HSM serial partials) under NDA.

4) Key rotation: We support automatic scheduled rotation (configurable cadence), manual rotation via API, and dual-key or staggered rotation to achieve near-zero downtime. For cached KV (model KV cache and prefix caches) our runtime supports a rewrap strategy: when a master key rotates, we re-encrypt data keys and continue serving with the new key while honoring existing cached contexts until they expire or are proactively flushed. We include a rotation plan and playbook in the onboarding docs.

5) TLS & client connections: Minimum TLS 1.2 supported; TLS 1.3 preferred and enabled by default for all public endpoints. We prefer ECDHE cipher suites with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305. Mutual TLS (mTLS) is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments (customer-provided certs via ACME or managed cert rotation). Certificate rotation is automated for hosted endpoints; customers manage certs in Private.

6) Evidence & attestation: We can provide:
  - SOC 2 Type II report excerpts (redacted)
  - Cloud KMS attestations (links to provider HSM attestation pages)
  - HSM vendor attestation + serials for Private deployments (under NDA)

Attachments included: redwood_kms_hsm_faq.pdf (detailed Q&A), certificate_matrix.csv (TLS/cipher mapping per endpoint).

Great — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers first, then links and next steps: 

• Key policy template: Attached is a minimal AWS KMS key policy and an example IAM role that we recommend (see link to HubSpot doc in related_links). We only request kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey for the short-lived unwrap operation; the customer maintains full control of key policies.

• FIPS attestation: Yes — we accept FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or FIPS 140-3 attestation for on-prem HSMs. During onboarding we will collect vendor-signed attestation and HSM identifiers. Lauren (compliance) will manage the NDAs and artifact exchange.

• Default rotation cadence: For hosted keys the default is 365 days if the customer does not configure a cadence. We include sample API calls in the FAQ (redwood_kms_hsm_faq.pdf) — the manual rotate is a single API call to issue a rewrap and then a key-state transition; we can walk through this in the demo.
